To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the NF2 gene is a tumor suppressor gene which encodes a band 4. 1-related protein schwannomin.
NF2 is the first structural protein identified as a tumor suppressor and the NF2 gene is mutated in NF2 and a majority of schwannomas and sporadic meningiomas.
NF2 gene encodes a new type of tumor suppressor that is involved in cell differentiation and growth control.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the NF2 tumor suppressor gene and its protein product, schwannomin.
the molecular mechanisms involved in the development of NF2 and the identification of the biological function of the NF2 protein.
elucidating the function of this novel tumor gene in order to provide insight into the pathogenesis of NF2 and to provide new therapeutic approaches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NF2 gene is involved in the suppression of tumors in the CNS, but not in the peripheral nerves, and that this is a novel mechanism of tumor suppression.
NF2 is a novel mechanism of tumor suppression and that schwannomin may play a key role in the control of cell proliferation, differentiation, migration, adhesion and polarity.
schwannomin is a tumor suppressor which acts through a new mechanism of growth control, i.e. by modulating the cytoskeleton and cell adhesion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NF2 is a tumor suppressor gene which encodes a protein involved in cell differentiation, adhesion and motility, and which may be involved in embryonic development.
NF2 is a new tumor suppressor gene which is inactivated by somatic mutations in a variety of sporadic and NF2 associated tumors.
NF2 gene mutations in schwannomas and other NF2-related tumors are common and that the NF2 gene product schwannomin has a novel function in the cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NF2 is an important model to understand the molecular basis of tumor suppression.
NF2 is a new mechanism of growth suppression and that the protein encoded by this gene may be a structural component of the cytoskeleton.
NF2 is an important model for tumor suppression and a paradigm shift in the way we look at tumor suppressors.
